title: Diaper rash: soothe and when to call
summary: Most diaper rash improves with air time and barrier cream. Some patterns need a look.
whatsNormal:
Diaper rash is red, irritated skin in the diaper area from wetness, stool, or friction.

• Mild pinkness that improves within 1–2 days of home care is common
• Change diapers often and clean gently, pat dry, do not rub hard
• Air time without a diaper helps healing
• Thick zinc oxide barrier cream after each change protects skin

Breastfed stool can be frequent and acidic, more changes usually help more than harsh wipes.
watchFor: Rash spreading beyond the diaper area or into skin folds
Rash not improving after 2–3 days of consistent home care
Baby seems in pain with every diaper change
callDoctorIf: Bright red rash with satellite spots (small red dots nearby), possible yeast
Pus, honey-colored crusts, or fever with rash
Rash with bloody stool or severe diarrhea
You are unsure, a photo for your pediatrician's nurse line is a good start
